claims.text: The FeNiCrCoCu coating on Cu is a stable FCC solid solution at 300 K.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating has a low initial dislocation density at 300 K.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating has well-defined, stable stacking-fault structures at 300 K.
Elevated temperature causes a thermally activated shift from dislocation-mediated plasticity to rapid lattice disordering in FeNiCrCoCu.
The critical mechanism shift occurs when the thermal condition exceeds the spinodal decomposition temperature.
Crossing the critical temperature collapses stacking-fault stability.
Crossing the critical temperature produces a surge in dislocation density that outpaces strain hardening.
Heating and deformation transform stable Shockley partials into unstable full dislocations and amorphous-like regions.
High-strain deformation combined with thermal softening triggers a clustering-to-ordering or disordering transition.
Compression induces a clustering-to-ordering transition in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
FeNiCrCoCu rapidly loses short-range order at elevated temperature.
Collapse of the stacking-fault barrier causes a surge in dislocation mobility.
Loss of strain-hardening ability causes severe wear.
Wear resistance and elastic modulus decline sharply above the critical temperature.
Wear depth and coefficient of friction increase suddenly above the critical temperature.
At 300 K, lattice distortion controls dislocation motion and stacking faults provide strain hardening.
Tribo-oxidation is not the dominant protective mechanism in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 forms a protective spinel layer under elevated-temperature wear.
A critical threshold near 840 K, or broadly above 800 K, can be inferred for FeNiCrCoCu from similar Al-containing systems.
Above the critical temperature, the coating changes from an ordered or dislocation-pinned state to a highly disordered, low-hardness state with high dislocation density.
